findings.claim: Introduced by the correction. The CI sensing step the proposal gives as an example, `devai sense run --preset baseline --as-role engineer --write`, will not create any reading in DEVAI 1.5.6, so `sensor-integrity` would still scan 0. The installed runtime shows three problems. First, `sense run` only accepts `--preset`, `--round`, `--repo-root`, `--input`, `--dry-run` and `--human` (release-host.js:219138-219140), plus `--as-role`/`--authority-session` added by the authority boundary (197293); there is no `--write`. Second, `executeResolvedSenseSelection` (219088) only writes the reading to stdout. Its resolution declares `implicit_persistence: false` (191063), and `sense-presets.json` sets `implicit_persistence: "forbidden"`. The only writers to `.devai/state/sensor-readings/<kind>` are `sense record --input` (`recordSensorReading`, 218676, effect `harness-write`) and `sense record --rebuild` (218537). Third, the action-level effect of `sense run` is `remote-write` (capabilities `fs:f5-state`, `fs:proofs`, `proc:dynamic`, `net:sensor-runtime`; 12861-12890 and 177610), not the preset's `local-write`/`harness-write` as the text says. The conditional block ('se o verbo não materializar leituras válidas… bloqueados') prevents an empty check from being approved. But A1-2 asks the Owner to approve a step whose command, source and effect class are wrong. That was exactly the subject of cycle-1 high 4.
findings.fix: Describe the step as the chain the runtime actually supports: `devai sense run --preset baseline --repo-root . --as-role <papel>` (action effect `remote-write`, aggregate preset effect `local-write`), capturing each member's `SensorReading` from stdout. Then one `devai sense record --input <arquivo> --as-role <papel>` per reading (`harness-write`, writing to `.devai/state/sensor-readings/<kind>`). Only after that, `check --only sensor-integrity` with `readings_scanned > 0`. Remove `--write` from the example. State in A1-2 the effect class of each verb and the role that is allowed to run it in CI. Keep the block clause if the rehearsal does not produce valid readings.
